prompt:
I need the front end for Freshwatch. An in-house monitoring tool built by the business-intelligence team at a regional grocery chain to track whether its published sales and operations reports are fresh, correct and loading, and to alert the right person when they aren't.

Who's using it: Tomás Reyes, a BI platform engineer on the analytics team at Harlow & Pine Markets, a 310-store chain. He's on call this week and knows the data pipelines well.

What they're doing right now: It's Monday at 6:40am. At 8am, regional operations directors will review the weekly sales report. Overnight, Freshwatch raised 3 alerts. The weekly sales report shows Northeast region revenue down 41% week-over-week, which could be a real event (a weekend storm closed stores) or a late point-of-sale feed. The shrink report failed to refresh. A labor-hours report is loading slowly. He has to decide what's real, what to escalate to the ops directors before 8, what to mute, and whether to tighten the rule that let a known late feed fire a false alarm last month.

What's in the system at this point: There are 240 published reports, each with an owner, refresh schedule, upstream tables, last successful refresh time and typical viewer count; the weekly sales report has 180 Monday viewers. There are 46 alert rules covering freshness, row-count deviation, metric swing over 25% and load time over 12s, plus 5 active mute rules. Alerts in the last 24 hours: 14 total, 3 unacknowledged. The Northeast POS feed landed 71% of the expected rows by 5:00am; on average it completes by 4:15am. A weather note shows 23 Northeast stores closed Saturday. The shrink report failed at 3:02am with a source-table permission error. The on-call rotation shows Tomás this week and Priya Natarajan next week.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
